Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 1242 PM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

- Mostly cloudy and mild today and Tuesday. Near record high
  temperatures Tuesday. 

- Mild conditions continue Wednesday with increasing potential for
  light rain.

&&

.AVIATION...

A complex of low pressure spans the entire Plains states into 
central Canada today, and this is the focus of aviation conditions 
in the Great Lakes today through Tuesday. The system has a primary 
low center near the SD/MN border with a warm front extending into 
the Ohio valley that is accumulating a generous supply of moisture 
drawn northward from the Gulf coast. A broad expanse of MVFR ceiling 
is the result which is moving northward across southern Lower Mi 
this afternoon. These clouds settle into IFR this evening with some 
pockets of drizzle as the low level jet ramps up. Drizzle is better 
added to the forecast as observational trends dictate, however the 
IFR mention has plentiful support from the Ohio valley to the 
Midwest. 

A south to north break back into VFR follows across the area
late tonight and Tuesday morning as the system warm sector builds 
into the region. Model projections capture the pattern reasonably 
well and bring VFR ceiling up toward MBS during Tuesday morning. The 
current MS valley moisture axis then feeds additional clouds into the
warm sector for sub 5000 ft VFR during the afternoon north of DTW. 
Warm sector boundary layer mixing also leads to SW gusts near 30 
knots from mid afternoon into Tuesday evening. 

For DTW... MVFR ceiling solidifies this afternoon and then drops 
into IFR this evening until a transition back to VFR late tonight or 
early Tuesday morning. The VFR return is initially ceiling below 
5000 ft which becomes scattered during Tuesday afternoon. 

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* High for ceilings 5000 ft or less this afternoon and tonight. 
  Moderate to low Tuesday.
